title: In 1889, a 30-Foot Wall of Water Hit a Town at 40 mph

scenes.text: A thirty-foot wave hit a town at forty miles an hour.
scenes.keywords: flood wall of water river valley

scenes.text: A dam failed above Johnstown, Pennsylvania, at ten past three on May thirty-first.
The water raced fourteen miles down a narrow valley. It reached the town in under an hour.
It swept away sixteen hundred homes.
Then fires broke out in the wreckage.
In all, 2,209 people died. It happened in 1889.
scenes.keywords: flood aftermath town black and white

description:
In 1889, a wall of water about thirty feet high hit Johnstown, Pennsylvania at up to forty miles an hour.
The South Fork Dam failed, and the flood killed 2,209 people and destroyed about 1,600 homes.
Had you heard of the Johnstown Flood?
first_comment: The water took about 57 minutes to travel from the dam to the town. Would you have heard the warning?
